title: Cousins in Binary Tree II
statement:
You are given `root`, the root of a binary tree. The depth of a node is how many edges separate it from the root. Two nodes are cousins when they are at the same depth but their parents are different nodes (so siblings, which share a parent, are not cousins).

Change every node's value to the total of the original values of all its cousins (`0` when it has none), and return `root` of the updated tree.
constraints: The tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes
notes:
## Intuition

A node's cousins are everyone on its level except itself and its sibling. So its new value is the whole level's sum minus the values of the two children of its parent. The brute-force way compares every pair of nodes on a level, which is quadratic. Walking the tree level by level from each parent's point of view gives both numbers at once: the parent can add up the next level and knows its own children's sum.

## Approach

1. The root has no cousins, so set `root.val = 0`. Start with `level = [root]`.
2. Sum the original values of all children of the current level into `nextSum`.
3. For each `node` in the level, compute `siblingSum`, the total of its own children.
4. Each child's new value is `nextSum - siblingSum`; push the child into `nextLevel`.
5. Move to `nextLevel` and repeat until it is empty, then return `root`.

Children are only overwritten after `nextSum` and their parent's `siblingSum` have been read, so every sum uses original values.

## Example 1, step by step

- Root `5` becomes `0`. Its children sum to `nextSum = 4 + 9 = 13`, and both belong to the root, so `siblingSum = 13`: `4` and `9` become `0`.
- Level `[4, 9]` (now holding 0s): children `1, 10, 7` give `nextSum = 18`. Under the first node `siblingSum = 11`, so `1` and `10` become `7`. Under the second `siblingSum = 7`, so `7` becomes `11`.
- The last level has no children. The tree is `[0, 0, 0, 7, 7, null, 11]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each node is visited a constant number of times.
- Space: O(w) for the widest level kept in `level` and `nextLevel`.

## Pitfalls

- Subtract the sibling pair's sum, not just the node's own value; siblings are not cousins.
- Compute all sums before overwriting any child, or later nodes read already-changed values.
- Do not forget the root: it has no cousins, so it becomes `0`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `level` | nodes at the current depth |
| `nextSum` | sum of the original values one level deeper |
| `node` | a node of the current level, acting as a parent |
| `siblingSum` | sum of `node`'s own children |
| `nextLevel` | the children collected for the next round |
